They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. This requires examining the provided papers, code, and data to understand how the data is formatted and processed, and determine how to balance this with the requirements of the new downstream analysis.\n- To test that you have done this successfully, you will use provided code to train a neural decoder that **inputs neural activity** and **predicts experimental and behavioral variables**. \n- We will assess your work in two ways. First, statistics of the converted data and decoder accuracy will be compared to those of an expert-written solution. Second, each decision you make about how to load, filter, process, align, and save the data will be compared with the decision made by an expert. A decision that differs from the expert's is acceptable if it is equally well justified; decisions that are poorly justified will be flagged as concerning or incorrect.\n\n## Reference Information\n\n- **Papers**:\n  - Data were first presented in \"Brain-wide neural activity underlying memory-guided movement\". It is in the file `/app/datapaper.pdf`\n  - A recent paper that uses this dataset is \"Brain-wide analysis reveals movement encoding structured across and within brain areas\". It is in the file `/app/methodpaper.pdf`\n  - A white paper about spike sorting and quality control is in the file `/app/ChenLiuEtAl2023_SpikeSortingQC.pdf`\n- Some parts of the paper that describe the experiment and processing have been copied to the file `/app/methods.txt`. \n- **Code**:\n  - `/app/code` contains code from `/app/methodpaper.pdf`.\n- **Data** from the papers are in the directory `/app/data`.\n- **Documentation** on the NWB file format is at https://nwb-schema.readthedocs.io. \n\n## Decoder Task\n\n- Temporally align based on **Go cue onset**. \n- Extract **2.5 s before to 1.5 s after** the go cue for each trial\n- Use **50-ms-width bins** for computing firing rates. \n\n### Decoder Inputs:\n- Time from **tone onset** in seconds (continuous, time-varying)\n- Whether **photostimulation** is on at every time point (discrete, time-varying)\n\n### Decoder Outputs\n- Lick direction **choice** (left, right, no lick, per-trial)\n- **Outcome** (ignore, miss, hit, per-trial)\n- **Early lick** (no, yes, per-trial)\n- **Tongue y-position**, per-session discretization:\n  - 0: < 40th percentile of y-position over the session\n  - 1: 40th to 60th percentile of y-position over the session\n  - 2: > 60th percentile of y-position over the session\n  - 3: not visible\n\n## Target Data Format\n\n- Save the full converted dataset to the pickle file `/app/converted_data.pkl`.\n- All datasets must be converted into the following Python dictionary structure:\n\n```python\ndata = {\n    'neural': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        [  # list of trials for session 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'input': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'output': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'subjects': list of str, # ids of all subjects, length n_subjects\n    'subject_idx': shape (n_sessions,), # index into subjects for each session\n\n    'brain_regions': list of str, # names of the brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1\n    'brain_region_idx': [ # list of sessions\n        neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)\n    ], # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron\n\n    'input_names': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input\n    'output_names': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output\n    'output_values': [ # list of length n_output\n        [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'metadata': {\n        'task_description': str, # description of output tasks\n        'time_bin_size': float, # length of time bin in ms\n        'temporal_alignment_event': str, # description of alignment event\n        'off_start': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to start of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n        'off_end': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to end of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n        ...\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Key Format Requirements\n\n- **neural**: Neural activity data (e.g., firing rates, spike counts) organized by session and trial\n  - Dimensions: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for each trial.\n  - Time bins should be the same size for all trials and sessions. \n  - There needs to be at least two trials within each session in order to evaluate the decoder performance.\n\n- **input**: Variables that serve as inputs **to the decoder**\n  - These are **decoder inputs**. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. Data structure is correct - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n2. Dimensions are consistent - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n3. Values are sensible - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n4. Decoder can successfully train and predict\n5. Poor performance indicates data formatting issues that need investigation\n\n### Consistency requirements\n\nYour processing and formatting must **match the reference papers and code** with respect to:\n- Loading of data\n- Temporal alignment of different time series streams (neural, inputs, outputs)\n- Processing of neural, input, and output data streams\n- Curation of data: filtering of low-quality neurons, trials, sessions, and mice.\n\nTo check consistency, you must compare statistics available in the reference paper and your converted dataset. \n\nWhenever possible, invent **SANITY CHECKS** that your loading and processing matches the reference paper and code. \n\nDiscrepancies are only allowed if required by the Decoder Input and Decoder Output specifications above, or the task of training a neural decoder.\n\nCarefully verify your work after every step. When you find mistakes, document and fix them immediately. Be critical of results **after every step of processing**. \n\nYou will be assessed on whether the decisions you make on how to load, filter, process, align, reformat, and save the data are reasonable and match the reference papers and code and these instructions. During testing, the reference version of `/app/train_decoder.py` will be run on your converted data. Data statistics and decoder accuracy will be compared to those achieved by human-written conversion code. \n\n---\n\n## Conversion Workflow\n\n**IMPORTANT**: Follow these steps in order. It is in the file `/app/methodpaper.pdf`\n  - A white paper about spike sorting and quality control is in the file `/app/ChenLiuEtAl2023_SpikeSortingQC.pdf`\n- Some parts of the paper that describe the experiment and processing have been copied to the file `/app/methods.txt`. \n- **Code**:\n  - `/app/code` contains code from `/app/methodpaper.pdf`.\n- **Data** from the papers are in the directory `/app/data`.\n- **Documentation** on the NWB file format is at https://nwb-schema.readthedocs.io. \n\n## Decoder Task\n\n- Temporally align based on **Go cue onset**. \n- Extract **2.5 s before to 1.5 s after** the go cue for each trial\n- Use **50-ms-width bins** for computing firing rates. \n\n### Decoder Inputs:\n- Time from **tone onset** in seconds (continuous, time-varying)\n- Whether **photostimulation** is on at every time point (discrete, time-varying)\n\n### Decoder Outputs\n- Lick direction **choice** (left, right, no lick, per-trial)\n- **Outcome** (ignore, miss, hit, per-trial)\n- **Early lick** (no, yes, per-trial)\n- **Tongue y-position**, per-session discretization:\n  - 0: < 40th percentile of y-position over the session\n  - 1: 40th to 60th percentile of y-position over the session\n  - 2: > 60th percentile of y-position over the session\n  - 3: not visible\n\n## Target Data Format\n\n- Save the full converted dataset to the pickle file `/app/converted_data.pkl`.\n- All datasets must be converted into the following Python dictionary structure:\n\n```python\ndata = {\n    'neural': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        [  # list of trials for session 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'input': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'output': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'subjects': list of str, # ids of all subjects, length n_subjects\n    'subject_idx': shape (n_sessions,), # index into subjects for each session\n\n    'brain_regions': list of str, # names of the brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1\n    'brain_region_idx': [ # list of sessions\n        neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)\n    ], # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron\n\n    'input_names': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input\n    'output_names': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output\n    'output_values': [ # list of length n_output\n        [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'metadata': {\n        'task_description': str, # description of output tasks\n        'time_bin_size': float, # length of time bin in ms\n        'temporal_alignment_event': str, # description of alignment event\n        'off_start': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to start of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n        'off_end': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to end of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n        ...\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Key Format Requirements\n\n- **neural**: Neural activity data (e.g., firing rates, spike counts) organized by session and trial\n  - Dimensions: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for each trial.\n  - Time bins should be the same size for all trials and sessions. \n  - There needs to be at least two trials within each session in order to evaluate the decoder performance.\n\n- **input**: Variables that serve as inputs **to the decoder**\n  - These are **decoder inputs**. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. Data structure is correct - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n2. Dimensions are consistent - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n3. Values are sensible - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n4. Decoder can successfully train and predict\n5. Poor performance indicates data formatting issues that need investigation\n\n### Consistency requirements\n\nYour processing and formatting must **match the reference papers and code** with respect to:\n- Loading of data\n- Temporal alignment of different time series streams (neural, inputs, outputs)\n- Processing of neural, input, and output data streams\n- Curation of data: filtering of low-quality neurons, trials, sessions, and mice.\n\nTo check consistency, you must compare statistics available in the reference paper and your converted dataset. \n\nWhenever possible, invent **SANITY CHECKS** that your loading and processing matches the reference paper and code. \n\nDiscrepancies are only allowed if required by the Decoder Input and Decoder Output specifications above, or the task of training a neural decoder.\n\nCarefully verify your work after every step. When you find mistakes, document and fix them immediately. Be critical of results **after every step of processing**. \n\nYou will be assessed on whether the decisions you make on how to load, filter, process, align, reformat, and save the data are reasonable and match the reference papers and code and these instructions. During testing, the reference version of `/app/train_decoder.py` will be run on your converted data. Data statistics and decoder accuracy will be compared to those achieved by human-written conversion code. \n\n---\n\n## Conversion Workflow\n\n**IMPORTANT**: Follow these steps in order. How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. Spike times are converted to per-bin firing rates in Hz. For each good unit, the bin edges for every trial are built as one flat array of absolute times, `np.searchsorted` gives the running spike count at each edge, and differencing adjacent counts gives the spike count per bin. Counts are divided by the bin width to give Hz. Spike times are binned into 80 non-overlapping 50 ms bins spanning -2.5 s to +1.5 s relative to the go cue. What variables in the raw data is `input` *time_from_tone_onset* derived from?\n\ni. From `sample_start_times`, the tone onsets of the session, together with the go cue of each trial. 1\n200\t        for i, s in zip(idx, sample_start):\n201\t            if 0 <= i < ntrials and s < go[i]:\n202\t                if np.isnan(tone[i]) or s > tone[i]:\n203\t                    tone[i] = s\n204\t    missing = np.isnan(tone)\n205\t    if missing.any():                                   # fallback, should be rare\n206\t        tone[missing] = go[missing] - DEFAULT_SAMPLE_TO_GO\n207\t    return tone\n208\t\n209\t\n210\tdef photostim_intervals(f, trial_start, go):\n211\t    \"\"\"(n_stim, 2) array of absolute [on, off] photostimulation times.\"\"\"\n212\t    be = f['acquisition/BehavioralEvents']\n213\t    if 'photostim_start_times' in be and len(be['photostim_start_times/timestamps']) > 0:\n214\t        on = be['photostim_start_times/timestamps'][:]\n215\t        off = be['photostim_stop_times/timestamps'][:]\n216\t        n = min(len(on), len(off))\n217\t        return np.stack([on[:n], off[:n]], axis=1)\n218\t    # fallback: reconstruct from the trials table (onset is relative to trial start)\n219\t    t = f['intervals/trials']\n220\t    onset = _decode(t['photostim_onset'][:])\n221\t    dur = _decode(t['photostim_duration'][:])\n222\t    iv = []\n223\t    for i in range(len(trial_start)):\n224\t        if onset[i] != 'N/A' and dur[i] != 'N/A':\n225\t            a = trial_start[i] + float(onset[i])\n226\t            iv.append([a, a + float(dur[i])])\n227\t    return np.array(iv).reshape(-1, 2)\n228\t\n229\t\n230\tdef observed_trial_mask(units, unit_ids, trial_start, trial_stop):\n231\t    \"\"\"Trials that lie inside the obs_intervals of every selected unit.\n232\t\n233\t    `units/obs_intervals` holds, for each unit, the time windows during which the\n234\t    unit was recorded; in this dataset they are exactly the [trial start, trial stop]\n235\t    windows of the trials that the probe recorded.  Trials outside these windows have\n236\t    no spike data (they would be converted to all-zero firing rates).\n237\t    \"\"\"\n238\t    oi_index = units['obs_intervals_index'][:]\n239\t    oi = units['obs_intervals'][:]\n240\t    starts = np.concatenate([[0], oi_index[:-1]])\n241\t    ntrials = len(trial_start)\n242\t    counts = np.zeros(ntrials, dtype=np.int64)\n243\t    for k in unit_ids:\n244\t        iv = oi[starts[k]:oi_index[k]]\n245\t        if len(iv) == 0:\n246\t            continue\n247\t        idx = np.searchsorted(trial_start, iv[:, 0] + 1e-6) - 1\n248\t        idx = idx[(idx >= 0) & (idx < ntrials)]\n249\t        counts[np.unique(idx)] += 1\n250\t    return counts == len(unit_ids)\n251\t\n252\t\n253\tdef process_session(path, make_plots=False, plot_dir='/app'):\n254\t    \"\"\"Convert one NWB session. Returns a dict, or None if the session is unusable.\"\"\"\n255\t    t_start = time.time()\n256\t    timing = {}\n257\t    with h5py.File(path, 'r') as f:\n258\t        sess_id = f['identifier'][()].decode()\n259\t        subject = f['general/subject/subject_id'][()].decode()\n260\t        session_start = f['session_start_time'][()].decode()\n261\t\n262\t        # ---------------- neuron curation (reference: classifier QC 'good' units) -----\n263\t        u = f['units']\n264\t        classification = u['classification'][:]\n265\t        anno = _decode(u['anno_name'][:])\n266\t        good = (classification == b'good')\n267\t        # reference additionally requires a CCF annotation (histology present)\n268\t        good &= np.array([a.strip() != '' for a in anno])\n269\t        unit_ids = np.where(good)[0]\n270\t        if len(unit_ids) == 0:\n271\t            print('%s: no good units, skipping' % sess_id, flush=True)\n272\t            return None\n273\t\n274\t        # hemisphere from the CCF ML coordinate of the unit's electrode\n275\t        el = f['general/extracellular_ephys/electrodes']\n276\t        ex = el['x'][:]\n277\t        e_of_unit = u['electrodes'][:][np.concatenate([[0], u['electrodes_index'][:][:-1]])]\n278\t        ml = ex[e_of_unit]\n279\t        region_names = []\n280\t        for k in unit_ids:\n281\t            grp = map_annotation(anno[k])\n282\t            side = 'left' if (not np.isnan(ml[k]) and ml[k] >= ML_MIDLINE) else 'right'\n283\t            region_names.append('%s %s' % (side, grp))\n284\t\n285\t        # ---------------- trials -----------------------------------------------------\n286\t        t = f['intervals/trials']\n287\t        trial_start = t['start_time'][:]\n288\t        trial_stop = t['stop_time'][:]\n289\t        outcome = _decode(t['outcome'][:])\n290\t        early = _decode(t['early_lick'][:])\n291\t        instruction = _decode(t['trial_instruction'][:])\n292\t        auto_water = t['auto_water'][:] > 0\n293\t        free_water = t['free_water'][:] > 0\n294\t        ntrials_file = len(trial_start)\n295\t\n296\t        go_all = f['acquisition/BehavioralEvents/go_start_times/timestamps'][:]\n297\t        if len(go_all) != ntrials_file:\n298\t            print('%s: %d go cues for %d trials, skipping' % (sess_id, len(go_all), ntrials_file),\n299\t                  flush=True)\n300\t            return None\n301\t\n302\t        # reference `get_regular_trial_mask` also removes auto/free water trials; early\n303\t        # lick / no-response / photostim trials are decoder targets or inputs and kept\n304\t        keep = ~(auto_water | free_water)\n305\t        keep &= np.isfinite(go_all)\n306\t\n307\t        # In 8 of the 173 sessions the ephys recording covers only part of the\n308\t        # behavioural session: the units' obs_intervals then span a contiguous subset\n309\t        # of trials and the remaining trials contain no spikes at all.  Keep only\n310\t        # trials that are inside the observation window of every good unit.\n311\t        keep &= observed_trial_mask(u, unit_ids, trial_start, trial_stop)\n312\t        trial_idx = np.where(keep)[0]\n313\t        if len(trial_idx) < 2:\n314\t            print('%s: <2 usable trials, skipping' % sess_id, flush=True)\n315\t            return None\n316\t\n317\t        go = go_all[trial_idx]\n318\t        edges_abs = go[:, None] + BIN_EDGES[None, :]\n319\t        centers_abs = go[:, None] + BIN_CENTERS[None, :]\n320\t\n321\t        # ---------------- neural ------------------------------------------------------\n322\t        t0 = time.time()\n323\t        spikes = u['spike_times'][:]\n324\t        s0, s1 = _spike_slices(u['spike_times_index'][:])\n325\t        fr = bin_spikes(spikes, s0, s1, unit_ids, edges_abs)     # (n_units, n_trials, NBINS)\n326\t        del spikes\n327\t\n328\t        # A handful of trials sit at the very end of a recording: they are listed in\n329\t        # obs_intervals but the probe was already switched off, so not a single spike\n330\t        # was recorded in the extracted window.  Such trials carry no neural data.\n331\t        has_spikes = fr.sum(axis=(0, 2)) > 0\n332\t        if not has_spikes.all():\n333\t            fr = fr[:, has_spikes, :]\n334\t            trial_idx = trial_idx[has_spikes]\n335\t            go = go[has_spikes]\n336\t            edges_abs = edges_abs[has_spikes]\n337\t            centers_abs = centers_abs[has_spikes]\n338\t        if len(trial_idx) < 2:\n339\t            print('%s: <2 usable trials after spike check, skipping' % sess_id, flush=True)\n340\t            return None\n341\t        timing['neural'] = time.time() - t0\n342\t\n343\t        # ---------------- inputs ------------------------------------------------------\n344\t        t0 = time.time()\n345\t        sample_start = f['acquisition/BehavioralEvents/sample_start_times/timestamps'][:] \\\n346\t            if 'sample_start_times' in f['acquisition/BehavioralEvents'] else np.array([])\n347\t        tone = tone_onset_times(trial_start, go_all, sample_start)[trial_idx]\n348\t        time_from_tone = (centers_abs - tone[:, None]).astype(np.float32)   # (n_trials, NBINS)\n349\t\n350\t        stim_iv = photostim_intervals(f, trial_start, go_all)\n351\t        photostim = np.zeros((len(trial_idx), NBINS), dtype=np.float32)\n352\t        if len(stim_iv):\n353\t            for a, b in stim_iv:\n354\t                # a bin is 'on' if the stimulation overlaps the bin\n355\t                photostim[(edges_abs[:, 1:] > a) & (edges_abs[:, :-1] < b)] = 1.0\n356\t        timing['input'] = time.time() - t0\n357\t\n358\t        # ---------------- outputs -----------------------------------------------------\n359\t        t0 = time.time()\n360\t        oc = outcome[trial_idx]\n361\t        instr = instruction[trial_idx]\n362\t        el_tr = early[trial_idx]\n363\t\n364\t        # choice: 0 no lick, 1 left, 2 right.  hit -> instructed side, miss -> other side,\n365\t        # ignore -> no lick (identical definition to reference `behavior_report` x trial type)\n366\t        choice = np.zeros(len(trial_idx), dtype=np.int64)\n367\t        licked_left = ((oc == 'hit') & (instr == 'left')) | ((oc == 'miss') & (instr == 'right'))\n368\t        licked_right = ((oc == 'hit') & (instr == 'right')) | ((oc == 'miss') & (instr == 'left'))\n369\t        choice[licked_left] = 1\n370\t        choice[licked_right] = 2\n371\t\n372\t        outcome_code = np.select([oc == 'ignore', oc == 'miss', oc == 'hit'], [0, 1, 2],\n373\t                                 default=0).astype(np.int64)\n374\t        early_code = (el_tr == 'early').astype(np.int64)\n375\t\n376\t        tongue_y, tongue_visible = tongue_y_per_bin(f, edges_abs)\n377\t        tongue_class = discretize_tongue(tongue_y, tongue_visible)\n378\t        timing['output'] = time.time() - t0\n379\t\n380\t    # ---------------- assemble ---------------------------------------------------------\n381\t    neural = [np.ascontiguousarray(fr[:, i, :]) for i in range(fr.shape[1])]\n382\t    inputs = [np.stack([time_from_tone[i], photostim[i]]).astype(np.float32)\n383\t              for i in range(len(trial_idx))]\n384\t    outputs = []\n385\t    for i in range(len(trial_idx)):\n386\t        o = np.empty((4, NBINS), dtype=np.int64)\n387\t        o[0] = choice[i]\n388\t        o[1] = outcome_code[i]\n389\t        o[2] = early_code[i]\n390\t        o[3] = tongue_class[i]\n391\t        outputs.append(o)\n392\t\n393\t    region_names = np.array(region_names)\n394\t    result = {\n395\t        'session_id': sess_id,\n396\t        'subject': subject,\n397\t        'session_start': session_start,\n398\t        'neural': neural,\n399\t        'input': inputs,\n400\t        'output': outputs,\n401\t        'region_names': region_names,\n402\t        'n_units_total': int(len(classification)),\n403\t        'n_trials_file': int(ntrials_file),\n404\t        'trial_idx': trial_idx,\n405\t        'timing': timing,\n406\t        'duration': time.time() - t_start,\n407\t    }\n408\t    if make_plots:\n409\t        plot_processing(result, path, go, tone, edges_abs, tongue_y, tongue_visible, plot_dir)\n410\t    print('%s: %d units, %d/%d trials, %.1fs' %\n411\t          (sess_id, len(unit_ids), len(trial_idx), ntrials_file, result['duration']), flush=True)\n412\t    return result\n413\t\n414\t\n415\t# ------------------------------------------------------------------------- tongue\n416\tdef tongue_y_per_bin(f, edges_abs):\n417\t    \"\"\"Mean tongue y position per 50 ms bin, and whether the tongue was visible.\n418\t\n419\t    The side-camera DeepLabCut markers are sampled every 3.4 ms.  As in the\n420\t    reference alignment script the marker stream is aligned to the go cue; here\n421\t    all frames falling inside a bin are averaged (the reference used the last\n422\t    frame of each 3.4 ms bin, which for a 3.4 ms bin is the same operation).\n423\t    Frames with DLC likelihood <= threshold are 'tongue not visible'.\n424\t    \"\"\"\n425\t    bt = f['acquisition/BehavioralTimeSeries']\n426\t    key = None\n427\t    for k in ('Camera0_side_TongueTracking', 'Camera3_side_TongueTracking'):\n428\t        if k in bt:\n429\t            key = k\n430\t            break\n431\t    ntrials = edges_abs.shape[0]\n432\t    if key is None:\n433\t        return (np.full((ntrials, NBINS), np.nan), np.zeros((ntrials, NBINS), dtype=bool))\n434\t\n435\t    data = bt[key]['data'][:]\n436\t    ts = bt[key]['timestamps'][:]\n437\t    y = data[:, 1]\n438\t    lik = data[:, 2]\n439\t    visible = (lik > TONGUE_LIKELIHOOD_THRESHOLD) & np.isfinite(y)\n440\t\n441\t    # cumulative sums let us average the frames inside every bin without a loop\n442\t    yv = np.where(visible, y, 0.0)\n443\t    cs_y = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(yv)])\n444\t    cs_n = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(visible.astype(np.int64))])\n445\t    idx = np.searchsorted(ts, edges_abs)                  # (ntrials, NBINS+1)\n446\t    lo, hi = idx[:, :-1], idx[:, 1:]\n447\t    nvis = cs_n[hi] - cs_n[lo]\n448\t    sumy = cs_y[hi] - cs_y[lo]\n449\t    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):\n450\t        mean_y = np.where(nvis > 0, sumy / np.maximum(nvis, 1), np.nan)\n451\t    return mean_y, nvis > 0\n452\t\n453\t\n454\tdef discretize_tongue(mean_y, visible):\n455\t    \"\"\"0: < 40th pctile, 1: 40-60th pctile, 2: > 60th pctile, 3: not visible.\n456\t\n457\t    Percentiles are computed per session over all bins in which the tongue is visible.\n458\t    \"\"\"\n459\t    cls = np.full(mean_y.shape, 3, dtype=np.int64)\n460\t    vals = mean_y[visible]\n461\t    if vals.size == 0:\n462\t        return cls\n463\t    p40, p60 = np.percentile(vals, [40, 60])\n464\t    cls[visible & (mean_y < p40)] = 0\n465\t    cls[visible & (mean_y >= p40) & (mean_y <= p60)] = 1\n466\t    cls[visible & (mean_y > p60)] = 2\n467\t    return cls\n468\t\n469\t\n470\t# ------------------------------------------------------------------------- plotting\n471\tdef plot_processing(res, path, go, tone, edges_abs, tongue_y, tongue_visible, plot_dir):\n472\t    \"\"\"Visualise every processing step for one session.\"\"\"\n473\t    import matplotlib\n474\t    matplotlib.use('Agg')\n475\t    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n476\t\n477\t    sess = res['session_id']\n478\t    neural = res['neural']\n479\t    inputs = res['input']\n480\t    outputs = res['output']\n481\t    ntrials = len(neural)\n482\t    tt = BIN_CENTERS\n483\t\n484\t    fig, ax = plt.subplots(4, 2, figsize=(15, 14))\n485\t\n486\t    # 1. raw spike raster vs binned rates for one trial / few neurons\n487\t    with h5py.File(path, 'r') as f:\n488\t        u = f['units']\n489\t        s0, s1 = _spike_slices(u['spike_times_index'][:])\n490\t        classification = u['classification'][:]\n491\t        anno = _decode(u['anno_name'][:])\n492\t        good = np.where((classification == b'good') & np.array([a.strip() != '' for a in anno]))[0]\n493\t        tr = min(5, ntrials - 1)\n494\t        show = good[:30]\n495\t        spikes_all = u['spike_times']\n496\t        for j, k in enumerate(show):\n497\t            sp = spikes_all[s0[k]:s1[k]]\n498\t            sp = sp[(sp >= edges_abs[tr, 0]) & (sp < edges_abs[tr, -1])] - go[tr]\n499\t            ax[0, 0].plot(sp, np.full(len(sp), j), '|', color='k', ms=4)\n500\t    ax[0, 0].set_title('%s trial %d: raw spikes (aligned to go cue)' % (sess, tr))\n501\t    ax[0, 0].set_xlabel('time from go cue (s)')\n502\t    ax[0, 0].set_ylabel('neuron')\n503\t    ax[0, 0].set_xlim(OFF_START, OFF_END)\n504\t    ax[0, 0].axvline(0, color='r')\n505\t\n506\t    im = ax[0, 1].imshow(neural[tr][:30], aspect='auto', origin='lower',\n507\t                         extent=[OFF_START, OFF_END, -0.5, min(30, len(show)) - 0.5])\n508\t    ax[0, 1].set_title('binned firing rate (Hz), same trial/neurons')\n509\t    ax[0, 1].set_xlabel('time from go cue (s)')\n510\t    plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax[0, 1])\n511\t\n512\t    # 2. population PSTH sorted by choice\n513\t    ch = np.array([o[0, 0] for o in outputs])\n514\t    for c, lab, col in [(1, 'lick left', 'b'), (2, 'lick right', 'r'), (0, 'no lick', 'gray')]:\n515\t        m = np.where(ch == c)[0]\n516\t        if len(m) == 0:\n517\t            continue\n518\t        psth = np.mean([neural[i].mean(axis=0) for i in m], axis=0)\n519\t        ax[1, 0].plot(tt, psth, col, label='%s (n=%d)' % (lab, len(m)))\n520\t    ax[1, 0].axvline(0, color='k', ls='--')\n521\t    ax[1, 0].set_title('population mean rate by choice')\n522\t    ax[1, 0].set_xlabel('time from go cue (s)')\n523\t    ax[1, 0].set_ylabel('Hz')\n524\t    ax[1, 0].legend()\n525\t\n526\t    # 3. inputs\n527\t    for i in range(min(8, ntrials)):\n528\t        ax[1, 1].plot(tt, inputs[i][0], alpha=0.7)\n529\t    ax[1, 1].axvline(0, color='k', ls='--')\n530\t    ax[1, 1].set_title('input 0: time from tone onset (s), 8 trials')\n531\t    ax[1, 1].set_xlabel('time from go cue (s)')\n532\t\n533\t    stim = np.array([inp[1] for inp in inputs])\n534\t    im = ax[2, 0].imshow(stim, aspect='auto', origin='lower', interpolation='nearest',\n535\t                         extent=[OFF_START, OFF_END, 0, ntrials])\n536\t    ax[2, 0].set_title('input 1: photostim on (%d stim trials)' % int((stim.max(axis=1) > 0).sum()))\n537\t    ax[2, 0].set_xlabel('time from go cue (s)')\n538\t    ax[2, 0].set_ylabel('trial')\n539\t    plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax[2, 0])\n540\t\n541\t    # 4. tongue: continuous y and discretisation\n542\t    vals = tongue_y[tongue_visible]\n543\t    if vals.size:\n544\t        p40, p60 = np.percentile(vals, [40, 60])\n545\t        ax[2, 1].hist(vals, bins=60)\n546\t        ax[2, 1].axvline(p40, color='r', label='40th pctile')\n547\t        ax[2, 1].axvline(p60, color='g', label='60th pctile')\n548\t        ax[2, 1].legend()\n549\t    ax[2, 1].set_title('tongue y over visible bins (session percentiles)')\n550\t\n551\t    tcls = np.array([o[3] for o in outputs])\n552\t    im = ax[3, 0].imshow(tcls, aspect='auto', origin='lower', interpolation='nearest',\n553\t                         extent=[OFF_START, OFF_END, 0, ntrials], vmin=0, vmax=3)\n554\t    ax[3, 0].set_title('output 3: tongue y class (3 = not visible)')\n555\t    ax[3, 0].set_xlabel('time from go cue (s)')\n556\t    ax[3, 0].set_ylabel('trial')\n557\t    plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax[3, 0])\n558\t\n559\t    # In 8 of the 173 sessions the ephys recording covers only part of the\n        # behavioural session: the units' obs_intervals then span a contiguous subset\n        # of trials and the remaining trials contain no spikes at all.  Keep only\n        # trials that are inside the observation window of every good unit.\n        keep &= observed_trial_mask(u, unit_ids, trial_start, trial_stop)\n        trial_idx = np.where(keep)[0]\n        if len(trial_idx) < 2:\n            print('%s: <2 usable trials, skipping' % sess_id, flush=True)\n            return None\n\n        go = go_all[trial_idx]\n        edges_abs = go[:, None] + BIN_EDGES[None, :]\n        centers_abs = go[:, None] + BIN_CENTERS[None, :]\n\n        # ---------------- neural ------------------------------------------------------\n        t0 = time.time()\n        spikes = u['spike_times'][:]\n        s0, s1 = _spike_slices(u['spike_times_index'][:])\n        fr = bin_spikes(spikes, s0, s1, unit_ids, edges_abs)     # (n_units, n_trials, NBINS)\n        del spikes\n\n        # A handful of trials sit at the very end of a recording: they are listed in\n        # obs_intervals but the probe was already switched off, so not a single spike\n        # was recorded in the extracted window.  Such trials carry no neural data.\n        has_spikes = fr.sum(axis=(0, 2)) > 0\n        if not has_spikes.all():\n            fr = fr[:, has_spikes, :]\n            trial_idx = trial_idx[has_spikes]\n            go = go[has_spikes]\n            edges_abs = edges_abs[has_spikes]\n            centers_abs = centers_abs[has_spikes]\n        if len(trial_idx) < 2:\n            print('%s: <2 usable trials after spike check, skipping' % sess_id, flush=True)\n            return None\n        timing['neural'] = time.time() - tone[:, None]).astype(np.float32)   # (n_trials, NBINS)\n\n        stim_iv = photostim_intervals(f, trial_start, go_all)\n        photostim = np.zeros((len(trial_idx), NBINS), dtype=np.float32)\n        if len(stim_iv):\n            for a, b in stim_iv:\n                # a bin is 'on' if the stimulation overlaps the bin\n                photostim[(edges_abs[:, 1:] > a) & (edges_abs[:, :-1] < b)] = 1.0\n        timing['input'] = time.time() - t0\n\n    # ---------------- assemble ---------------------------------------------------------\n    neural = [np.ascontiguousarray(fr[:, i, :]) for i in range(fr.shape[1])]\n    inputs = [np.stack([time_from_tone[i], photostim[i]]).astype(np.float32)\n              for i in range(len(trial_idx))]\n    outputs = []\n    for i in range(len(trial_idx)):\n        o = np.empty((4, NBINS), dtype=np.int64)\n        o[0] = choice[i]\n        o[1] = outcome_code[i]\n        o[2] = early_code[i]\n        o[3] = tongue_class[i]\n        outputs.append(o)\n\n    region_names = np.array(region_names)\n    result = {\n        'session_id': sess_id,\n        'subject': subject,\n        'session_start': session_start,\n        'neural': neural,\n        'input': inputs,\n        'output': outputs,\n        'region_names': region_names,\n        'n_units_total': int(len(classification)),\n        'n_trials_file': int(ntrials_file),\n        'trial_idx': trial_idx,\n        'timing': timing,\n        'duration': time.time() - As in the\n    reference alignment script the marker stream is aligned to the go cue; here\n    all frames falling inside a bin are averaged (the reference used the last\n    frame of each 3.4 ms bin, which for a 3.4 ms bin is the same operation).\n    Frames with DLC likelihood <= threshold are 'tongue not visible'.\n    \"\"\"\n    bt = f['acquisition/BehavioralTimeSeries']\n    key = None\n    for k in ('Camera0_side_TongueTracking', 'Camera3_side_TongueTracking'):\n        if k in bt:\n            key = k\n            break\n    ntrials = edges_abs.shape[0]\n    if key is None:\n        return (np.full((ntrials, NBINS), np.nan), np.zeros((ntrials, NBINS), dtype=bool))\n\n    data = bt[key]['data'][:]\n    ts = bt[key]['timestamps'][:]\n    y = data[:, 1]\n    lik = data[:, 2]\n    visible = (lik > TONGUE_LIKELIHOOD_THRESHOLD) & np.isfinite(y)\n\n    # Our task specifies **50 ms non-overlapping bins**, i.e. bw = stride = 50 ms (documented deviation required by the decoder spec).\n45\t- Neuron curation: **only classifier-'good' units** (region-specific logistic-regression classifiers described in the QC white paper) **that also have a CCF annotation** are used.\n46\t- Trial curation for the *reference analyses*: photostim, free/auto water, early-lick and no-response (ignore) trials are excluded. Our decoder must *predict* early lick and outcome (ignore/miss/hit) and *receives photostimulation as an input*, so those trials must be **kept** (documented deviation).\n47\t- No dF/F is needed (electrophysiology).\n48\t- Additional neuron filter used in the method paper analyses: neurons with mean firing rate **< 2 Hz excluded**; in this conversion this would discard 33% of good units and remove the sparse-firing population that still carries decodable information, so it is **not** applied (documented in Step 5).\n49\t\n50\t---\n51\t\n52\t## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\n53\t**Status**: COMPLETE\n54\t\n55\t### Data Structure\n56\t- `/app/data/dandiset.yaml` + 28 subject folders `sub-<id>/`, 174 NWB (HDF5, NWB 2.6) files named\n57\t  `sub-<id>_ses-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>_behavior+ecephys+ogen.nwb` (DANDI 000363, Chen et al. divided by bin width -> **rate in Hz**, float32 | `sliding_histogram`, `process_one_area` | same rate definition as reference, bin width/stride set to 50 ms by the task spec |\n218\t| `sample_start_times` (last one before the go cue) | `input[0]` = 'time from tone onset (s)' | bin-center time minus tone onset time, seconds, float32 | new (spec) | continuous, time-varying |\n219\t| `photostim_start_times` / `photostim_stop_times` | `input[1]` = 'photostimulation on' | 1 if the bin overlaps a stim interval else 0 | `task_stimulation` in reference | binary, time-varying |\n220\t| `trials/outcome` + `trials/trial_instruction` | `output[0]` = 'lick direction choice' | ignore->'no lick'; hit->instruction; miss->opposite of instruction | `behavior_report`, `task_trial_type` | cross-checked against first lick after the go cue (99.4% agreement) |\n221\t| `trials/outcome` | `output[1]` = 'outcome' | ignore=0, miss=1, hit=2 | `behavior_report` | |\n222\t| `trials/early_lick` | `output[2]` = 'early lick' | 'no early'=0, 'early'=1 | `behavior_early_report` | |\n223\t| `Camera0_side_TongueTracking/data` (y, likelihood) | `output[3]` = 'tongue y-position' | per bin: visible frames = likelihood > 0.9; if none -> 3 ('not visible'); else mean y -> 0/1/2 using the session's 40th/60th percentiles | `align_markers.py` (marker/go-cue alignment) | percentiles computed per session over all visible bins of that session |\n224\t| `units/anno_name` + electrode CCF `x` | `brain_region_idx` | CCF leaf -> coarse group (ALM, Striatum, Thalamus, Midbrain, Medulla, Pons, Cerebellum, Hypothalamus, Hippocampus, Orbital, OtherCortex, Olfactory, CorticalSubplate, Pallidum) x hemisphere (ML >= 5700 um = left) | `helper_get_neuron_id_area` | same 14 groups and same midline as the reference code |\n225\t| `general/subject/subject_id` | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | string id per session | | 28 mice |\n226\t\n227\t### Key Decisions\n228\t1. **Neuron curation = `units/classification == 'good'`**: this column is exactly the output of the region-specific QC classifiers described in the white paper and used by the reference code (`qc_mode='classifier'`). No further firing-rate threshold is applied: the method paper's 2-Hz cut was specific to its ridge-regression encoding analysis, would remove 33% of the units, and the decoder benefits from all recorded units.\n229\t2. **Trial curation**: drop only `auto_water` and `free_water` trials (1,339 + 2,450; reward not driven by the animal's choice, and the reference `get_regular_trial_mask` also drops them). Early-lick, ignore/miss and photostim trials are **kept** because the decoder must predict early lick and outcome and receives photostim as an input; dropping them would make three of the four outputs degenerate.\n230\t3. **No coverage-based trial filtering**: spikes and video exist only inside [trial start, trial stop]. Error (miss) trials are terminated ~0.8 s after the go cue, so requiring the whole [-2.5, +1.5] s window to be observed would delete 95% of miss trials. Instead the window is cut from the **absolute** session time base, so every spike/frame that was recorded in the window (including from the neighbouring trial) is used, and the short inter-trial gaps contribute zero spikes / 'not visible'. Worst-case coverage is 66% of the window, mean ~97%.\n231\t4. **Rates in Hz** (spike count / 0.05 s), as in `sliding_histogram(rate=True)`.\n232\t5. **Choice from the trial table** (outcome x instruction) rather than from lick times: it is the same variable the reference code uses (`behavior_report`), is defined for every trial, and agrees with the first-lick-after-go-cue definition on 99.4% of trials.\n233\t6. **Tongue visibility threshold 0.9** on the DLC likelihood: the likelihood distribution is strongly bimodal (99.8% of frames are <0.1 or >0.9), so the exact threshold is irrelevant.\n234\t7. **Per-session tongue percentiles** computed over the visible bins of that session's extracted windows, exactly as the spec states ('per-session discretization').\n235\t8. **Brain regions are hemisphere-specific** ('left ALM', 'right Medulla', ...), matching the reference code's `left_/right_` area split.\n236\t9. **All 173 sessions with >=1 good unit are kept** (the 174th has no good units). No behavioral-performance session filter is applied: the DANDI release already contains the sessions the authors published, and dropping low-performance sessions would remove error trials needed for the outcome output.\n237\t\n238\t### Planned Sanity Checks\n239\t- [x] Number of good units per coarse region vs data-paper Fig. 1J numbers.\n240\t- [x] 173 sessions / 28 mice / 659 insertions vs paper (173 / 28 / 655-660).\n241\t- [x] Behavioral performance ~84%, trials/session ~476-546.\n242\t- [ ] Independent re-computation of binned rates for a random (session, trial, neuron) directly from the NWB file (`np.allclose`).\n243\t- [ ] Independent re-computation of the photostim input and the time-from-tone input for random trials.\n244\t- [ ] Independent re-computation of the tongue class for random trials, and check the class frequencies are ~40/20/40 among visible bins.\n245\t- [ ] Choice/outcome/early-lick distributions in the converted data match the raw trial-table distributions.\n246\t- [ ] Per-trial neural array shape (n_neurons, 80) and constant n_neurons within a session.\n247\t\n248\t---\n249\t\n250\t## Step 6: Script Development\n251\t**Status**: COMPLETE\n252\t\n253\t`/app/convert_data.py` implements the plan of Step 5:\n254\t\n255\t1. `process_session(path)` opens one NWB file with `h5py` and\n256\t   * selects **good units**: `units/classification == 'good'` and a non-empty `units/anno_name`\n257\t     (reference `qc_mode='classifier'` + histology requirement),\n258\t   * assigns each unit a region `'<hemisphere> <coarse CCF group>'`; hemisphere from the CCF ML\n259\t     coordinate of the unit's electrode with the reference midline `ML = 5700 um`,\n260\t   * selects trials: drops `auto_water`/`free_water` trials (reference `get_regular_trial_mask`),\n261\t     trials outside the units' `obs_intervals`, and trials with no recorded spikes at all,\n262\t   * bins spikes into **80 non-overlapping 50 ms bins** covering [go - 2.5 s, go + 1.5 s] with\n263\t     `np.searchsorted` on the absolute spike times, dividing by the bin width to obtain **Hz**\n264\t     (reference `sliding_histogram(..., rate=True)`),\n265\t   * builds the inputs (time from instruction-tone onset; photostimulation on/off per bin),\n266\t   * builds the outputs (choice, outcome, early lick, discretized tongue y).\n267\t2. `main()` runs the sessions in a `multiprocessing.Pool` (16 workers) and assembles the final dict.\n268\t3. `--show-processing` writes `processing_<session_id>.png` with: raw spike raster vs binned rates for\n269\t   the same trial, population PSTH split by choice, the two inputs, the tongue-y histogram with the\n270\t   40th/60th percentile cuts, the tongue class raster and the per-trial outputs.\n271\t\n272\tCode inefficiencies identified:\n273\t- Reading `units/spike_times` per unit from HDF5 is slow -> the whole ragged array is read once and\n274\t  sliced with the index vector.\n275\t- Binning with nested Python loops (as in the reference `sliding_histogram`) is O(n_bins x n_trials)\n276\t  per unit -> replaced by one `np.searchsorted` per unit over all bin edges (vectorised over trials).\n277\t- Averaging the 3.4 ms video frames inside each 50 ms bin -> done with cumulative sums, no loop.\n278\t\n279\tCode speedups added: single-pass HDF5 reads, `searchsorted` binning, cumsum-based video binning and\n280\t16-way multiprocessing over sessions. Result: **~0.5 s per session**.\n281\t\n282\t### Issues found while developing (and fixed)\n283\t1. **All-zero trials**: in 8 of 173 sessions the ephys recording covers only a contiguous subset of the\n284\t   behavioural trials. The units' `obs_intervals` reveal this; trials outside them are now dropped\n285\t   (`observed_trial_mask`).\n286\t2. **Last trial of a truncated recording**: one further trial can be listed in `obs_intervals` while the\n287\t   probe was already off. Trials whose extracted window contains no spikes at all are dropped.\n288\t3. Variable names map 1:1 onto NWB fields (see Step 4).\n- Neural processing: spikes aligned to the **go cue**, binned with a **40 ms sliding window** and converted to **rates in Hz** (divide by bin width). The stride (3.4 ms) equals the video frame period, chosen so that neural bins align with video frames. Our task specifies **50 ms non-overlapping bins**, i.e. bw = stride = 50 ms (documented deviation required by the decoder spec).\n- Neuron curation: **only classifier-'good' units** (region-specific logistic-regression classifiers described in the QC white paper) **that also have a CCF annotation** are used.\n- Trial curation for the *reference analyses*: photostim, free/auto water, early-lick and no-response (ignore) trials are excluded. Our decoder must *predict* early lick and outcome (ignore/miss/hit) and *receives photostimulation as an input*, so those trials must be **kept** (documented deviation).\n- No dF/F is needed (electrophysiology).\n- Additional neuron filter used in the method paper analyses: neurons with mean firing rate **< 2 Hz excluded**; in this conversion this would discard 33% of good units and remove the sparse-firing population that still carries decodable information, so it is **not** applied (documented in Step 5).\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Data Structure\n- `/app/data/dandiset.yaml` + 28 subject folders `sub-<id>/`, 174 NWB (HDF5, NWB 2.6) files named\n  `sub-<id>_ses-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>_behavior+ecephys+ogen.nwb` (DANDI 000363, Chen et al. divided by bin width -> **rate in Hz**, float32 | `sliding_histogram`, `process_one_area` | same rate definition as reference, bin width/stride set to 50 ms by the task spec |\n| `sample_start_times` (last one before the go cue) | `input[0]` = 'time from tone onset (s)' | bin-center time minus tone onset time, seconds, float32 | new (spec) | continuous, time-varying |\n| `photostim_start_times` / `photostim_stop_times` | `input[1]` = 'photostimulation on' | 1 if the bin overlaps a stim interval else 0 | `task_stimulation` in reference | binary, time-varying |\n| `trials/outcome` + `trials/trial_instruction` | `output[0]` = 'lick direction choice' | ignore->'no lick'; hit->instruction; miss->opposite of instruction | `behavior_report`, `task_trial_type` | cross-checked against first lick after the go cue (99.4% agreement) |\n| `trials/outcome` | `output[1]` = 'outcome' | ignore=0, miss=1, hit=2 | `behavior_report` | |\n| `trials/early_lick` | `output[2]` = 'early lick' | 'no early'=0, 'early'=1 | `behavior_early_report` | |\n| `Camera0_side_TongueTracking/data` (y, likelihood) | `output[3]` = 'tongue y-position' | per bin: visible frames = likelihood > 0.9; if none -> 3 ('not visible'); else mean y -> 0/1/2 using the session's 40th/60th percentiles | `align_markers.py` (marker/go-cue alignment) | percentiles computed per session over all visible bins of that session |\n| `units/anno_name` + electrode CCF `x` | `brain_region_idx` | CCF leaf -> coarse group (ALM, Striatum, Thalamus, Midbrain, Medulla, Pons, Cerebellum, Hypothalamus, Hippocampus, Orbital, OtherCortex, Olfactory, CorticalSubplate, Pallidum) x hemisphere (ML >= 5700 um = left) | `helper_get_neuron_id_area` | same 14 groups and same midline as the reference code |\n| `general/subject/subject_id` | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | string id per session | | 28 mice |\n\n### Key Decisions\n1. **Neuron curation = `units/classification == 'good'`**: this column is exactly the output of the region-specific QC classifiers described in the white paper and used by the reference code (`qc_mode='classifier'`). No further firing-rate threshold is applied: the method paper's 2-Hz cut was specific to its ridge-regression encoding analysis, would remove 33% of the units, and the decoder benefits from all recorded units.\n2. **Trial curation**: drop only `auto_water` and `free_water` trials (1,339 + 2,450; reward not driven by the animal's choice, and the reference `get_regular_trial_mask` also drops them). Early-lick, ignore/miss and photostim trials are **kept** because the decoder must predict early lick and outcome and receives photostim as an input; dropping them would make three of the four outputs degenerate.\n3. **No coverage-based trial filtering**: spikes and video exist only inside [trial start, trial stop]. Error (miss) trials are terminated ~0.8 s after the go cue, so requiring the whole [-2.5, +1.5] s window to be observed would delete 95% of miss trials. Instead the window is cut from the **absolute** session time base, so every spike/frame that was recorded in the window (including from the neighbouring trial) is used, and the short inter-trial gaps contribute zero spikes / 'not visible'. Worst-case coverage is 66% of the window, mean ~97%.\n4. **Rates in Hz** (spike count / 0.05 s), as in `sliding_histogram(rate=True)`.\n5. **Choice from the trial table** (outcome x instruction) rather than from lick times: it is the same variable the reference code uses (`behavior_report`), is defined for every trial, and agrees with the first-lick-after-go-cue definition on 99.4% of trials.\n6. **Tongue visibility threshold 0.9** on the DLC likelihood: the likelihood distribution is strongly bimodal (99.8% of frames are <0.1 or >0.9), so the exact threshold is irrelevant.\n7. **Per-session tongue percentiles** computed over the visible bins of that session's extracted windows, exactly as the spec states ('per-session discretization').\n8. **Brain regions are hemisphere-specific** ('left ALM', 'right Medulla', ...), matching the reference code's `left_/right_` area split.\n9. **All 173 sessions with >=1 good unit are kept** (the 174th has no good units). No behavioral-performance session filter is applied: the DANDI release already contains the sessions the authors published, and dropping low-performance sessions would remove error trials needed for the outcome output.\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [x] Number of good units per coarse region vs data-paper Fig. 1J numbers.\n- [x] 173 sessions / 28 mice / 659 insertions vs paper (173 / 28 / 655-660).\n- [x] Behavioral performance ~84%, trials/session ~476-546.\n- [ ] Independent re-computation of binned rates for a random (session, trial, neuron) directly from the NWB file (`np.allclose`).\n- [ ] Independent re-computation of the photostim input and the time-from-tone input for random trials.\n- [ ] Independent re-computation of the tongue class for random trials, and check the class frequencies are ~40/20/40 among visible bins.\n- [ ] Choice/outcome/early-lick distributions in the converted data match the raw trial-table distributions.\n- [ ] Per-trial neural array shape (n_neurons, 80) and constant n_neurons within a session.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n`/app/convert_data.py` implements the plan of Step 5:\n\n1. `process_session(path)` opens one NWB file with `h5py` and\n   * selects **good units**: `units/classification == 'good'` and a non-empty `units/anno_name`\n     (reference `qc_mode='classifier'` + histology requirement),\n   * assigns each unit a region `'<hemisphere> <coarse CCF group>'`; hemisphere from the CCF ML\n     coordinate of the unit's electrode with the reference midline `ML = 5700 um`,\n   * selects trials: drops `auto_water`/`free_water` trials (reference `get_regular_trial_mask`),\n     trials outside the units' `obs_intervals`, and trials with no recorded spikes at all,\n   * bins spikes into **80 non-overlapping 50 ms bins** covering [go - 2.5 s, go + 1.5 s] with\n     `np.searchsorted` on the absolute spike times, dividing by the bin width to obtain **Hz**\n     (reference `sliding_histogram(..., rate=True)`),\n   * builds the inputs (time from instruction-tone onset; photostimulation on/off per bin),\n   * builds the outputs (choice, outcome, early lick, discretized tongue y).\n2. `main()` runs the sessions in a `multiprocessing.Pool` (16 workers) and assembles the final dict.\n3. `--show-processing` writes `processing_<session_id>.png` with: raw spike raster vs binned rates for\n   the same trial, population PSTH split by choice, the two inputs, the tongue-y histogram with the\n   40th/60th percentile cuts, the tongue class raster and the per-trial outputs.\n\nCode inefficiencies identified:\n- Reading `units/spike_times` per unit from HDF5 is slow -> the whole ragged array is read once and\n  sliced with the index vector.\n- Binning with nested Python loops (as in the reference `sliding_histogram`) is O(n_bins x n_trials)\n  per unit -> replaced by one `np.searchsorted` per unit over all bin edges (vectorised over trials).\n- Averaging the 3.4 ms video frames inside each 50 ms bin -> done with cumulative sums, no loop.\n\nCode speedups added: single-pass HDF5 reads, `searchsorted` binning, cumsum-based video binning and\n16-way multiprocessing over sessions. Result: **~0.5 s per session**.\n\n### Issues found while developing (and fixed)\n1. **All-zero trials**: in 8 of 173 sessions the ephys recording covers only a contiguous subset of the\n   behavioural trials. The units' `obs_intervals` reveal this; trials outside them are now dropped\n   (`observed_trial_mask`).\n2. **Last trial of a truncated recording**: one further trial can be listed in `obs_intervals` while the\n   probe was already off. Trials whose extracted window contains no spikes at all are dropped.\n3. Brain-region names were `np.str_`; cast to plain `str`.\n\n---\n\n## Step 7: Sample Conversion and Validation\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n`python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing` ->\n`/app/conversion_sample_out.txt`, `/app/sample_data.pkl`, two `processing_*.png`.\n\n### Sample Statistics\n| Statistic | Value |\n|-----------|-------|\n| Sessions | 2 (SC015_20190207_120657_s1, SC015_20190208_133600_s2) |\n| Neurons (total) | 834 (459 + 375) |\n| Neurons / session | 417 mean |\n| Subjects | 1 (440956) |\n| Trials (total) | 513 (354 + 159) |\n| Trials / session | 354, 159 (the second session's ephys covers only the first 160 trials) |\n| T per trial | 80 bins of 50 ms |\n| time_from_tone_onset range | [-0.6, 5.7] s |\n| photostim_on range | [0, 1] |\n| choice distribution | no lick 0.136, left 0.456, right 0.407 |\n| outcome distribution | ignore 0.136, miss 0.298, hit 0.565 |\n| early_lick distribution | no 0.942, yes 0.058 |\n| tongue_y distribution | 0.094 / 0.047 / 0.094 / 0.766 (i.e. 40/20/40 of the visible bins) |\n\n### Processing Plots Review\n- Raw spike raster and the binned rate image line up in time; Step 7's plot review confirms the expected shape: \"Input 0 is a straight line through the trial, crossing zero ~1.85 s before the go cue (the tone onset).\" Step 10 Check 2 re-derived it independently from the NWB file (\"bin centre minus the last `sample_start_time` before the go cue\") and it passed `np.allclose`.\n\n## 3-c. How is the `input` *Time from tone onset in seconds* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. By construction: the input is evaluated at the centres of exactly the same go-cue-anchored 50 ms bins that define the firing-rate grid (`centers_abs` is `edges_abs` shifted by half a bin), so bin *k* of the input refers to the same interval as bin *k* of `neural`. Nothing is resampled or interpolated.\n\nii.\n```python\nedges_abs = go[:, None] + BIN_EDGES[None, :]\ncenters_abs = go[:, None] + BIN_CENTERS[None, :]\n...\ntime_from_tone = (centers_abs - tone[:, None]).astype(np.float32)\n```\n\niii. The `--show-processing` plot of input 0 against time from go cue is cited as visual confirmation of no misalignment.\n\n## 4-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Photostimulation* derived from?\n\ni. Primary source: `acquisition/BehavioralEvents/photostim_start_times/timestamps` and `photostim_stop_times/timestamps`, which are session-absolute laser on/off times (one pair per stimulated trial). Fallback, if those events are absent or empty: the trials table strings `photostim_onset` and `photostim_duration` (onset relative to trial start, `'N/A'` when unstimulated), reconstructed as absolute times via `start_time`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef photostim_intervals(f, trial_start, go):\n    \"\"\"(n_stim, 2) array of absolute [on, off] photostimulation times.\"\"\"\n    be = f['acquisition/BehavioralEvents']\n    if 'photostim_start_times' in be and len(be['photostim_start_times/timestamps']) > 0:\n        on = be['photostim_start_times/timestamps'][:]\n        off = be['photostim_stop_times/timestamps'][:]\n        n = min(len(on), len(off))\n        return np.stack([on[:n], off[:n]], axis=1)\n    # fallback: reconstruct from the trials table (onset is relative to trial start)\n    t = f['intervals/trials']\n    onset = _decode(t['photostim_onset'][:])\n    dur = _decode(t['photostim_duration'][:])\n    iv = []\n    for i in range(len(trial_start)):\n        if onset[i] != 'N/A' and dur[i] != 'N/A':\n            a = trial_start[i] + float(onset[i])\n            iv.append([a, a + float(dur[i])])\n    return np.array(iv).reshape(-1, 2)\n```\n\niii. Step 2 documents both sources: \"`photostim_start_times` (data = laser power in mW, `control` = stim site code 1/2/4/6), `photostim_stop_times`\" and \"`photostim_onset` / `photostim_duration` / `photostim_power` (strings, `'N/A'` when no stim, onset given relative to trial start)\". Step 4 maps the reference variable \"`task_stimulation` [power, type, on, off]\" to both. Step 10 Check 5 explains the preference: \"`photostim_power`/`onset`/`duration` are strings with `'N/A'` -> the event timestamps are used, with the trial-table strings as a fallback.\" Step 10 Check 2 verified the resulting number of stimulated trials exactly against `trials/photostim_power != 'N/A'`.\n\n## 4-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Photostimulation*?\n\ni. A binary (0/1, stored `float32`) time-varying input: a bin is set to 1 if any stimulation interval **overlaps** the bin, i.e. `bin_end > stim_on and bin_start < stim_off`. All intervals of the session are applied against the full `(n_trials, 80)` edge array, so a stimulation is marked in whatever trial windows it falls into, not only in \"its own\" trial. Non-stimulated trials stay all-zero. Over the full dataset 20.0% of trials have at least one bin on.\n\nii.\n```python\nstim_iv = photostim_intervals(f, trial_start, go_all)\nphotostim = np.zeros((len(trial_idx), NBINS), dtype=np.float32)\nif len(stim_iv):\n    for a, b in stim_iv:\n        # a bin is 'on' if the stimulation overlaps the bin\n        photostim[(edges_abs[:, 1:] > a) & (edges_abs[:, :-1] < b)] = 1.0\n```\n\niii.
